implementation: Store the K16 carry in one FP32 word, using either explicit bit normalization or unsigned-to-FP32 round-toward-zero conversion followed by exponent adjustment. Original product preparation, exponent choice, integer modulo sign decoding and ordered K16 truncation are preserved.

Only finite normal FP32 carries or zero and eligible BF16 operands enter the candidate. Subnormal, overflow and declined groups restart the original dot. No process or device rounding mode is changed.

Component headers have no product dispatcher include. Existing whole/CK providers, original QK arithmetic and dense/MoE replay implementations are byte-identical to the qualified source. The QKV harness alone enables the new six-way comparison.

QKV comparisons include all unrounded FP32 candidate values, all final BF16 cells, finite scratch writes, sorted common candidate ownership, input/index immutability and memory guards. The original selector PPB remains1000.
conclusions: The host arithmetic sweep checks40763392 normalization cases and1048576 ordered K16 groups per method with undefined-behavior and float-cast sanitizers. Native core checks2097152 ordered groups, including1214496 eligible and882656 fallback groups; all agree with the independent original arithmetic.

All24 generated projection cases,6264 raw dots and42 generated QK cases with96546912 score cells pass. The original q7169 QK comparison checks418496528 scores per variant,1255489584 total, and684 independent CPU dots, with zero raw-bit mismatches.

Completed q7169 QK time is341.5882ms for the qualified scalar-float route,315.7412ms for direct FP32 bits and314.1448ms for round-toward-zero; common key transpose is5.9128ms. The approximately27ms single-layer saving does not demonstrate a seconds-scale q8192 improvement.

Every QKV variant preserves58728448 external BF16 cells and3791742 unrounded candidate FP32 values. Completed preparation plus replay is52.8446/52.8659/52.5744ms for original/direct-bits/RTZ with4 lanes and1 staged group, and106.928/109.552/108.020ms for16 lanes and4 staged groups. Timings include raw capture writes and one warmup plus one measured sequence.

Keep FP32 carry outside product dispatch: exactness passes, while projection gains are negligible and the tested16-lane variants are slower. The cross-lane result motivates a separate investigation of current MoE work ownership; it is not MoE product evidence.
